_schema.purpose: The canonical, append-only per-position evidence record for v1.34's Phase 162 chip sweep (the 11-part v1.15 inventory run under `firestarter dev test <chip>` on Leonardo + Rev 2.0, v1.33 firmware). Sibling to bench/EVIDENCE.jsonl (the dual-arm WRV record, Phases 160-163): this file shares that record's nine-column locked core (locked_columns/locked_columns_note) so Phase 166's CLOSE-01 can assert the locked core uniformly across every milestone evidence file, while carrying its own v1.34-chip-sweep-specific evid_extension_columns set -- the dev-test-report-derived, provenance-derived and small human-judgement fields this sweep's own oracle (`dev test`, not a write/read/judge cycle) actually produces. One row per chip position (<cell_slug>__<arm>__<chip>, this file's own primary key shape). Plan 162-02 pins this schema; plans 162-05..162-10 append the ten primary v133 rows, the 2516 named-absence row, and any divergence-driven control re-run rows; Phase 165 classifies failures; Phase 166 closes out by reconciling row count against position_count_expected via close01_counting_rule and chip_sc04_rule.
_schema.locked_columns_note: locked_columns is the nine-column core pinned verbatim from bench/EVIDENCE.jsonl (itself pinned verbatim from .planning/v1.15/bench/EVIDENCE.json and .planning/v1.18/bench/EVIDENCE.json, where it is byte-identical) -- the stable core every milestone's evidence record has carried. evid_extension_columns is the Phase-162-specific set this chip sweep's own oracle (`firestarter dev test <chip>`, not a write/read/judge cycle) actually produces: dev-test-report-derived fields, provenance/config-dir fields shared with the WRV sibling, and the small set of human-supplied values/judgements this sweep needs that the WRV sweep does not (vpp_real_mv, prior_disposition, known_carried, reseat_count, divergence_verdict, jp4_position). The two-tier shape exists so Phase 166's close-out can assert on the locked core across every milestone's evidence file uniformly, while each sweep phase adds only the columns its own oracle produces -- observed extension keys in this file's rows are exactly the evid_extension_columns list, never the locked_columns list, and never a key outside either list.
_schema.jsonl_convention: One JSON object per line, LF line terminators, UTF-8 without ASCII escaping (ensure_ascii=False). Rows are emitted with keys in exactly record_keys order and are never sorted. This header object (keyed '_schema') is line 1 and is the ONLY line carrying the '_schema' key. No timestamp is recorded anywhere in this file -- not in this header, not in any row -- so a regeneration of bench/CHIP-EVIDENCE.md over an unchanged row set is byte-identical (see tools/render_chip_evidence.py --check). A row is never rewritten once appended: tools/render_chip_evidence.py's --append path asserts the existing prefix is byte-unchanged immediately before an atomic replace.
_schema.outcome_values_note: outcome_values is the identical two-value list under the field name tools/gate_record.py's check_outcome() already reads from a JSONL header (that tool is reused unmodified, not re-implemented here); outcome_domain is the same list under the name this plan pins for D-15/D-18. Both names carry the same value so gate_record.py's per-row domain check and this plan's own pinned field name are simultaneously satisfied from one source of truth.
_schema.outcome_semantics_note: validated here means fw_board_identity is non-null, the report was copied out of the frozen config dir with both copy SHAs matching their sources, and the config-dir invariant (check_arms.compute_config_dir_sha) held before and after the copy-out and removal -- and deliberately NOT anything about the chip's own step verdicts, because a `dev test` BAD is a result carried forward to Phase 165's triage as P-H2, never a skip. SC#1 counts a report artifact produced, not a passing report: if outcome were keyed on the chip's own verdict, the parts already known to fail (W27E512, W27E040, W29C040, AM27C020) would book as skips and Phase 165 would inherit four rows that look un-run rather than four rows holding a real, filed result.
_schema.close01_counting_rule: Computed over rows with arm=='v133' ONLY (arm=='control' rows are excluded per control_rerun_exclusion): (number of such rows with outcome=='validated') + (number of such rows with outcome=='skipped-with-reason') == position_count_expected (11), where 11 is the v1.15 physical inventory -- ten parts actually run (write scope for each defined by DERIVE-PLAN.json) plus the 2516's own named-absence row (named_absence_convention). The first term is 'positions holding a produced report artifact'; the second is 'positions holding a named reason for absence' (the 2516 row, or any other recorded skip -- never a blank). This equation is evaluated as a script over rows by Phase 166's CLOSE-01, never as a human count -- a silent gap between the row count and 11 is structurally visible as a nonzero remainder rather than something a reader has to notice.
_schema.chip_sc04_rule: Three conjoined identities, evaluated over rows, never counted by a human: (1) count(rows where arm=='control') == count(rows where arm=='v133' and divergence_verdict starts with 'diverges'); (2) every control row's control_rerun_for names an existing v133 row whose own divergence_verdict starts with 'diverges'; (3) no two control rows share the same control_rerun_for value. Total runs this cell records is stated as `10 + N` with N = count(arm=='control') -- ten primary parts run (the 2516 is a named absence, never run, so it contributes 0 to this term) plus N divergence-driven control re-runs -- which is a deliberate deviation from the roadmap's `11 + N` reading: the roadmap counted the 2516 as a run when D-06/D-14 in fact fixed it as a never-seated named absence, so this file's own arithmetic uses 10, not 11, as the run-count base while position_count_expected (the RECONCILIATION denominator, close01_counting_rule) correctly stays 11 (ten runs plus one named absence, both accounted-for).
_schema.control_rerun_exclusion: A row whose arm is 'control' is a divergence-arbitration re-run under D-17, not a sweep position -- it is excluded from the 11-position reconciliation (close01_counting_rule) and reconciled separately (chip_sc04_rule). This is the structural analogue of EVIDENCE.jsonl's BRINGUP- prefix exclusion, but keyed on `arm` rather than on a cell_id prefix: the chip sweep runs one cell (CHIP) for its whole run, so position_id's own __v133__/__control__ segment already keeps a control re-run's id distinct from the primary position it arbitrates, and a second exclusion mechanism keyed on a prefix would be redundant with the one this file already carries.
_schema.named_absence_convention: Exactly one row, chip == '2516', carries named_absence set and every machine-derived field as 'not measured — <reason>' (PD-10). Its arm reads 'v133' because that is the arm this phase was configured under, NOT because a run occurred against it -- the 2516 is never seated, read, or written in this phase. Its op reads 'not run — named absence', and that is the field a reader consults to learn the position was never attempted. It is counted by close01_counting_rule (as a 'skipped-with-reason', one of the 11 accounted-for positions) and it is NEVER counted by chip_sc04_rule, which only ever counts arm=='v133' rows whose divergence_verdict starts 'diverges' -- a named absence has no divergence_verdict to diverge from, and is never a candidate for a control re-run.
_schema.not_measured_convention: A reading that tooling blocks -- because a bootloader interrogation has not yet been recorded (judged_span_policy: PENDING-xshowvector on uno328pb), because a CLI path does not exist for a value, or for any other named reason -- is recorded as the string 'not measured — <reason>' (em dash or double-hyphen separator) with its blocking reason on the SAME line, never as a blank, null, or omitted field. tools/gate_record.py's field-presence check treats this exact shape as a valid, non-null value and rejects a bare 'not measured' with no reason.
_schema.negative_control_convention: A negative control (the W27C512 VPP-high init guard firing; the deliberate wrong-arm cross-flash producing a MISMATCH) is recorded as having FIRED -- the record states the guard/mismatch actually occurred and what happened next -- never merely as having been configured or made available. A mechanism that was present but never observed to fire is not evidence that it works. This file's own two examples: the MSG_ERR_VPP_HIGH init guard firing on a position where it was tripped deliberately or observed live, and D-10's nothing-was-filed proof (the dedup/off-TTY path never files an issue) -- recorded as an issue-count taken before and after, pasted as command output, never as an unverified assertion that nothing happened.
_schema.artifact_volume_policy_ref: bench/IMAGE-PLAN.json's top-level 'artifact_volume_policy' object -- the single home for what is committed vs. kept local vs. committed-on-failure across this milestone's bench artifacts (written images, read-back run_*.bin files, provenance JSON). Extended for this file's own artifact class: `dev test` report artifacts (bench/cells/CHIP/reports/<position_id>.{json,md}) are small, non-reproducible from any other record (the read runs that produced them are destroyed with the step, sha256_absence_note), and are COMMITTED UNCONDITIONALLY -- the commit-on-failure exception IMAGE-PLAN.json's policy carries for large binaries does not apply to them, and bench/.gitignore's `cells/*/reads/` and `cells/*/written.bin` entries do not cover `cells/*/reports/`. Stated explicitly here so a future reader does not apply the large-binary exception to a small, non-reproducible report artifact by analogy.
_schema.sha256_absence_note: sha256 is a PERMANENT named absence in every row of this file, because `dev test` retains no read image at all -- its read runs land in a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory destroyed with the step (chip_test.py's _dispatch_read), so there is no read artifact this appender could hash even in principle. Every row's sha256 therefore reads 'not measured — dev test retains no read image; the read runs are destroyed with the step. The report artifact SHAs are recorded in report_json_sha256/report_md_sha256.' Phase 166's CLOSE-01 locked-core assertion must accept this shape here: this is the ONLY milestone-evidence row family in the whole project whose sha256 column is a named absence rather than a real digest -- gate_record.check_required_fields already treats the 'not measured — <reason>' shape as a valid non-null value, so no gate change is needed, only this recorded expectation.
_schema.vpp_sign_convention: vpp_shortfall_mv = vpp_target_mv − vpp_firmware_mv, a positive value meaning the firmware's own measured VPP reading fell UNDER the chip's target voltage (rig-pins.json chips[chip].vpp_mv); a negative value means the firmware measured OVER target. This value is always computed by the appender from the other two columns and is never accepted as a CLI input (only vpp_real_mv, the operator's independent multimeter reading, is a human-supplied number, per PD-17).
_schema.prior_baseline_flag_semantics_note: PD-6's shared clause: five of the ten parts' newest recorded dispositions (see prior_disposition/prior_disposition_source on those rows) were obtained under a `write -b` invocation whose era semantics -- since withdrawn, Phase 145 D-17 -- BOTH skipped the blank-check AND skipped the erase (reference_write_b_skips_erase.md), not merely the blank-check its flag name suggests. Those five baselines were therefore taken under materially different flag semantics than exist on either the control or the v133 arm today, where `-b` is a forbidden_flags entry and every write in this milestone runs the full blank-check + erase + write + verify sequence. A divergence against one of those five baselines must be read with that difference in mind, not treated as a like-for-like comparison; this correction is also recorded in PROCEDURE.md's forbidden-invocation table.
